title: AP® U.S. History
subject: History
alignment: AP® United States History exam (unit order follows the usual course sequence; outline written in our own words)

units.title: Peoples of the Americas and first contacts, 1491–1607
objectives: Describe how Native American societies adapted to their environments before European contact
Explain the causes of European exploration and the effects of the Columbian Exchange
Compare Spanish, French and English goals and their dealings with Native peoples and Africans

units.title: Colonial societies, 1607–1754
objectives: Compare the economies, labor systems and religious life of the New England, Middle, Chesapeake and Southern colonies
Explain how slavery grew in the colonies and how enslaved people resisted it
Describe how trade and imperial policy tied the colonies to Britain

units.title: Revolution and a new republic, 1754–1800
objectives: Explain how the Seven Years' War and new British policies led to colonial resistance
Trace the ideas and events of the Revolution and the war for independence
Compare the Articles of Confederation with the Constitution and the debates over ratification
Describe the first party conflicts and foreign policy challenges of the new nation

units.title: Democracy, markets and reform, 1800–1848
objectives: Explain how voting rights and political parties changed in the early nineteenth century
Describe how the market revolution changed work, transportation and regional economies
Assess the goals and results of religious revival and reform movements, including abolition
Explain how removal policies affected Native American nations

units.title: Expansion, civil war and Reconstruction, 1844–1877
objectives: Explain how westward expansion intensified the conflict over slavery
Trace the political failures that led to secession
Explain why the Union won the Civil War and how emancipation changed its aims
Evaluate what Reconstruction achieved and why it ended

units.title: Industry, cities and the West, 1865–1898
objectives: Explain how big business, railroads and new technology transformed the economy
Describe the experiences of immigrants and workers and how labor organized
Explain how settlement of the West affected Native Americans and the environment
Compare responses to industrial change, including populism and the Gilded Age debates

units.title: Reform, empire, war and depression, 1890–1945
objectives: Explain the goals and results of the Progressive movement
Explain why the United States expanded overseas and entered the First World War
Describe cultural change in the 1920s and the causes of the Great Depression
Evaluate the New Deal and the effects of the Second World War at home and abroad

units.title: Cold War and a changing society, 1945–1980
objectives: Explain the goals of containment and how the Cold War shaped domestic life
Trace the strategies and achievements of the civil rights movement
Explain the causes and effects of the Vietnam War and the protest movements of the era
Describe the growth of new conservative and liberal movements

units.title: Recent America, 1980–present
objectives: Explain the rise of modern conservatism and its effects on government
Describe how the end of the Cold War and later conflicts changed foreign policy
Explain how technology, globalization, migration and demographic change reshaped American life
